verdict.rationale: Apple's own developer docs describe a local-AI stack aimed at Apple Silicon: MLX for training and fine-tuning generative models, Core ML for on-device inference, and PyTorch Metal backends for accelerated training on the Mac GPU. MLX is also documented as supporting Metal 4 and GPU Neural Accelerators. missing for 10: M4 Pro–specific runtime support documentation (the docs refer to Apple Silicon generically), evidence for third-party runtimes such as llama.cpp or ONNX Runtime, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, mainstream local-AI runtimes target this silicon — llama.cpp, MLX, ONNX Runtime, or the vendor's own AI software stack document support for its CPU, GPU, or NPU

citations.quote: MLX is an open-source array framework that lets you experiment with, training, researching, and fine-tuning generative models on Apple Silicon.
It supports Metal 4 and GPU Neural Accelerators for maximum performance
Accelerate the training of machine learning models in third-party frameworks right on your Mac with PyTorch backends.
Core ML delivers fast performance for integrating traditional machine learning models into your apps and games
